claims: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is the largest federal law enforcement agency under the Department of Homeland Security.
CBP is responsible for securing U.S. borders.
CBP is responsible for regulating international trade.
CBP is responsible for facilitating travel.
CBP officers and agents number over 60,000.
CBP officers and agents prevent illegal entry at ports of entry.
CBP officers and agents prevent drug smuggling at ports of entry.
CBP officers and agents prevent agriculture pests at ports of entry.
CBP's core mission is to secure U.S. borders against terrorists/weapons.
CBP's core mission is to enforce customs/immigration laws.
CBP's core mission is to manage trade.
CBP is comprised of the Office of Field Operations.
Office of Field Operations handles ports of entry.
CBP is comprised of U.S. Border Patrol.
U.S. Border Patrol handles areas between ports.
CBP is comprised of Air and Marine Operations.
CBP inspects over a million travelers daily.
CBP manages Preclearance programs at 15 international locations.
CBP was founded in 2003.
CBP was founded by bringing together agriculture specialists, customs officers, and border patrol agents.
